verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents an official CLI for managing tenant configuration, automating tasks, and fitting into deployment workflows. It also documents a Client Credentials flow meant for CLIs, daemons, and backend services that authenticate without a user, and a Terraform module for setting up tenant resources, so headless automation is clearly intended. However, the evidence never shows explicit CI pipeline setup or a documented non-interactive (credential-based) login for the CLI, so complete coverage of the story is not established. missing for 10: explicit CI/CD pipeline documentation, documented non-interactive CLI authentication for CI runners, details on what Agent Mode does, independent hands-on corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Learn how to use Auth0 CLI to manage your tenant configuration, automate tasks, and integrate Auth0 into your development and deployment workflows.
This flow is best suited for Machine-to-Machine (M2M) applications, such as CLIs, daemons, or backend services, because the system must authenticate and authorize the application instead of a user.
Set up apps, APIs, roles, MFA, enterprise SSO, and custom domains on Auth0 with a single Terraform module.
Agent Mode for the Auth0 CLI
